name: Lettuce

companions.note: Radishes deter soil pests and are harvested quickly, freeing space as lettuce grows
Compatible heights; kale provides slight wind shelter for lettuce in exposed beds

pnw_notes: Cool-season workhorse — one of the most rewarding succession crops in the PNW. Continuity is a butterhead that holds well without bolting. Succession sow every 2–3 weeks from March through May and again August through September for near-continuous harvest. Gets bitter in heat; summer sowing needs shade.

frost_hardiness.notes: Survives light frost; hard freeze causes mushy damage. Row cover essential below 28°F. Harvest quickly if a hard freeze is forecast.

planting_windows.notes: Succession sow every 2–3 weeks for continuous harvest
Fall window; heat-tolerant varieties extend into summer shoulder
Transplant starts for a head start on the season
Spring harvest; pick outer leaves or cut whole head at base
Fall/winter harvest; flavor improves with cold
